reason: Inspecting the sponsor-loaded tablet's hardware seems like a practical first step toward a request desk people can choose to use.
expectation: I expect the screwdriver to open the tablet for inspection or modification, though I don't yet know what it will reveal.

alternatives.reason: Preparing the receipt printer also seems useful, but the tablet is more directly connected to the listening concern.

effect: The listening app is removed and the microphone physically disconnected, so the tablet is ready to join the local network.
reaction: Disconnecting the microphone makes the privacy change concrete and satisfying.
reason: Connect the modified tablet to the local controller to build the request desk.
expectation: I expect the tablet to access local request services, though it may need further setup.

alternatives.reason: The printer will likely be useful for tickets, but I want to connect the tablet first.

effect: The tablet now uses the local controller and has no outside network route, keeping requests local unless the sender asks otherwise.
reaction: The explicit choice about passing requests on makes the privacy setup clearer.
reason: Add the large button to make the request tablet easier to use.
expectation: I expect the button to provide an accessible way to start a request, though its exact function is not yet clear.

alternatives.reason: The printer also needs preparing, but I want to finish the tablet controls first.

effect: The button sends only the request the user has chosen to write, making submission deliberate.
reaction: I like the clear distinction between standing at the desk and actually sending a request.
reason: Add the screen hood to give people more privacy while using the tablet.
expectation: I expect the hood to shield the screen from nearby observers.

alternatives.reason: The printer also needs paper, but I want to finish the tablet first.

effect: The hood shields the request form from the queue, completing another privacy measure.
reaction: A simple cardboard hood is a satisfyingly practical solution.
reason: Load the printer with paper to prepare it for the request desk; it's the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the printer to be ready to print request tickets, though it may need connecting or further setup.

effect: The printer feeds paper and can provide anonymous request identifiers.
reaction: The tear-off stubs are a practical privacy measure.
reason: Connect the printer to the local controller; it's the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the printer to become available for local request tickets, though it may need further setup.

effect: The printer now works locally, keeps return details off the shared queue, and supports clearing drafts and inspecting deletion settings.
reaction: The distinction between public queue information and private return details is useful.
reason: Combine the tablet and printer into a request desk; it's the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect a usable desk that lets people submit requests and receive a private identifier, though it may need further setup.

effect: The tablet and printer now form a private request desk, with a pencil option and no account required.
reaction: The non-digital option makes the desk feel more welcoming.
reason: Connect Moth to the desk; it's the only offered combination and may complete the request service.
expectation: I expect Moth to help handle requests with its source and correction controls, though I don't know exactly how.

effect: Moth's help is optional, and users can review or keep their own wording; the request desk goal is complete.
reaction: Sal keeping her original wording is a funny, concrete demonstration of user control.

mostWorthwhile.text: Disconnecting the microphone made the privacy promise tangible rather than relying on the sponsor's assurances.

leastWorthwhile.text: Loading and connecting the printer were practical but fairly routine, especially as each was the only offered combination.

surprise.text: The finished desk offered a pencil option as well as the tablet, so people needn't use an account or speak to a machine.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless; the offered combinations made each construction step clear, though I wasn't discovering compatibility myself.

continue.text: Yes. The practical privacy choices and Moth's optional help made me curious how the neighborhood will use its locally controlled infrastructure.
